source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: In Linux, Sanger, sanger and SANGER are the same file name.
explanation: Linux is case-sensitive, so they are three distinct files.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: What does an absolute path describe?

options.text: Every parent directory from the root down to the file
The path from the current working directory
The path to the home directory only

explanation: An absolute path starts at the root /; a relative path starts at the working directory.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

explanation: mkdir, rmdir and cd (with pwd and ls) manipulate directories; Ctrl+C ends a running program.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: What happens if you run rmdir on a directory that still contains files?

options.text: The directory and its files are removed
The files are moved to home

explanation: rmdir only removes empty directories; rm -r removes recursively.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: Which shell is the default on most Linux installations?
explanation: Bash is the default interactive shell on most Linux systems.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: Which one is not a Linux distribution named in the course?
explanation: Solaris is a separate UNIX variety; the others are Linux distributions.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux

stem: Linux is a clone of the original UNIX but does not contain its code.
explanation: Linux reimplements UNIX; it is free and open source.
source: CSC 582 Weeks 9 and 10, Basic Introduction to Linux
